name: Sweetcorn
grown_as: A tender annual grass grown for its cobs, sown in May under cover and planted out in a block (not a row) so the wind pollinates it. Kernel colour depends on the variety, usually yellow.
habit: A tall, upright, single stem 1.5 to 2 m, thick, solid and jointed like bamboo, with prop roots at the base. Long leaves arch out in two rows. A branched tassel at the very top; one or two cobs part-way up the stem.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate in two opposite rows, one leaf at each joint
leaf.outline: Long and strap-shaped, 50 to 100 cm by 5 to 10 cm, widest near the middle
leaf.base: A long sheath wrapping round the stem, with a small papery collar (ligule) where the blade bends away
leaf.tip: Tapering to a long point, often drooping
leaf.margin: Entire, finely rough, the edges often crinkled and wavy
leaf.veins: Parallel, running the length of the leaf, with a broad pale midrib down the centre
leaf.stalk: None: the sheath takes its place

flower.form: Two kinds on one plant: a branched male tassel at the top, and female silks hanging from the tip of the cob below
flower.colour: Tassel straw-yellow to purple-tinged; silks pale yellow-green, turning pink-brown
flower.centre: Tassel: many small spikelets on spreading branches, the stamens dangling and shedding pollen
flower.behind: The female cob wrapped in green leafy husks
flower.carried: The tassel standing above the top leaf. The cobs in the leaf joints halfway up the stem, wrapped in husks, a tuft of long silky threads hanging from each tip.
flower.size: Tassel 20 to 40 cm; silks 10 to 20 cm

fruit: A cob 15 to 20 cm in green husks, the silks at the tip dry and brown when ready. Inside: straight rows of plump, shiny, pale to golden yellow kernels packed on the core. Seed: a flattened wedge-shaped kernel, shrivelled and wrinkled in sweetcorn, yellow, about 8 to 10 mm.
seedling: A single rolled spear, then narrow grass-like leaves with blunt rounded tips; no seed leaves to be seen.
winter: Nothing: killed by frost and cleared

leaf: a long strap-shaped blade with parallel veins
bloom: a branched tassel with dangling stamens
or silks hanging from the tip of a husk-wrapped cob
seedling: a single narrow grass-like leaf with a blunt tip
young: long arching strap leaves in two rows
flower: a tassel at the top of the stem
silks from cobs in the leaf joints
crop: husk-wrapped cobs with brown silks on a tall stem
rows of yellow kernels where a husk is pulled back

look_alikes: Young sweetcorn can be taken for a big grass. Sorghum has its seeds in a head at the top, not in cobs.
